newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir crew finds new problems with oxygen system.
newsitem.headline: Mir crew finds new problems with oxygen system.

text.p: With just hours remaining before two relief cosmonauts reach the ailing Mir space station, the current crew concluded on Thursday that more time would be needed to repair the craft's oxygen system, Mission Control said.

"We have encountered new problems with the Elektron system. We have to stop now to take care of the (relief cosmonauts') docking, but we will keep trying to fix it afterwards," deputy flight director Viktor Blagov told Reuters.
The new problems appear to have been caused by blocked piping, which must be replaced rather than repaired, he said.

Blagov said the U.S. space shuttle Atlantis, due to dock with Mir in late September, would bring new piping and probably spare cable for a back-up system. Meanwhile, the Mir crew will try to revive the older, back-up Elektron, which is also off because it is in the Kvant-2 module, Blagov said.
The crew powered down Kvant-2 to save energy after Mir collided with a resupply ship on June 25, causing a major loss of power.
The crew hopes to bring in a separate power line to the Elektron in Kvant-2 if they can find a spare cable that fits.

"They will try to crank up the back-up Elektron, which is in working condition but is simply not connected to the power supply," Blagov said. "All they need is a spare cable to plug it in. We hope we will manage to find it on Mir."

The newer Elektron system in the Kvant-1 module has not worked for a week, and for several days the U.S. agency NASA has diagnosed the problem as coming from air bubbles or contaminant in the system lines. Repeated efforts to repair the unit have so far failed.
The Atlantis will also bring oxygen canisters for the Mir crew. Mir has three types of oxygen systems -- the two Elektron units, oxygen candles and canisters.

Blagov said the current situation was far from critical. "It is no tragedy, there is no reason to worry too much," he said. "They have enough oxygen to breathe now and they have enough oxygen in stock."

Blagov said the crew would continue burning oxygen "candles", which were the only source of oxygen on Mir when it first started orbiting the Earth 11 years ago. He said the present stocks would last at least 2-1/2 months.

The two relief cosmonauts, who are scheduled to dock with the Mir at 1703 GMT on Thursday, are due to don spacesuits on August 20 to perform repairs on Mir's Spektr module to restore power on the ailing ship. If these repairs succeed, then there will be enough energy to power up the entire Kvant-2 module.
